Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced a clearly authoritative source (Packet Clearing House IXP directory), so this row was moved to the full verification path. PCH confirms an active, government-run IXP (CGIX-BZV, Congo Internet eXchange) in Brazzaville, established 10 May 2013 and managed by regulator ARPCE. BGP/peering data (bgp.he.net) show active participation from Congo Telecom, MTN Congo, Airtel Congo, and ARPCE itself, alongside an international transit peer. Original score of 0/Unknown is corrected to 4.
revised_comments: The Republic of Congo has an operational Internet Exchange Point, CGIX-BZV (Congo Internet eXchange), based in Brazzaville and managed by the telecoms regulator ARPCE. Established in May 2013, it carries active peering from the country's main mobile and fixed operators, including Congo Telecom, MTN Congo and Airtel Congo, indicating an active IXP with moderate participation.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The cited source (dataprotection.africa/democratic-republic-of-the-congo) is for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, not the Republic of Congo (COG) — a country mismatch. The Republic of Congo in fact enacted Law No. 29-2019 on the Protection of Personal Data (10 October 2019, in force 25 November 2020), which the original 'No legislation' score overlooked. A National Commission for Personal Data is provided for in the Law but, per DLA Piper's 2024 update, had not yet been established (a project law to create it was approved by the Council of Ministers in July 2024 but not yet adopted). Score corrected from 1 (No legislation) to 3 (Legislation enacted but no enforcement authority).
revised_comments: The Republic of Congo has enacted comprehensive data protection legislation, Law No. 29-2019 on the Protection of Personal Data, passed on 10 October 2019 and in force since 25 November 2020. The Law establishes a National Commission for Personal Data to oversee enforcement, but as of 2024 this Commission had not yet been formally established, with implementing legislation still pending adoption.

Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.

revision_notes: Light check surfaced concrete evidence of startup activity (funding rounds, a dedicated VC fund and a recurring tech event), so this row was moved to the full verification path. Evidence found: Brazzaville-based delivery startup Noki Noki raised a $3m seed round in 2024; Fondation BantuHub and L'Archer Group launched a EUR 1m 'slow-build' VC fund for Congolese SMEs/startups in 2025-26; the annual OSIANE tech event (9th edition, 2025) convenes regional startups; a 2022 start-up label law exists but remains largely unimplemented (no decree, no labels issued). revised_comments: The Republic of Congo has an emerging but small tech startup ecosystem. Visible activity includes Brazzaville-based delivery platform Noki Noki, which raised a $3m seed round in 2024, and a new EUR 1m VC fund launched by Fondation BantuHub and L'Archer Group in 2025-26 targeting Congolese SMEs and startups. The annual OSIANE technology event, held in Brazzaville, has become a regional showcase for startups from the Congo Basin, and the government adopted a start-up label law in 2022, though its implementing decrees and formal labelling process have yet to take effect. Venture capital volumes and the number of active hubs remain limited compared with larger African markets.

revision_notes: Light check surfaced the university's own website confirming ICT/engineering degree programmes, so this row was moved to the full verification path. Marien Ngouabi University (the country's main public university) offers computer science/informatique and engineering degrees through its National School of Polytechnic Studies (ENSP), including electronics and telecommunications programmes and an engineering doctorate via a UNESCO Chair. Additional institutions with IT/CS or engineering programmes include the Congo University of Science and Technology, Denis Sassou Nguesso University, the private Higher Institute of Management and Technology (ISGT), and the Higher Institute of Technology of Central Africa (ISTAC). The national engineering research institute INRSIIT also exists. This constitutes several institutions with ICT/STEM offerings, though enrolment figures are not published. Original score of 0/Unknown is corrected to 3 (Moderate).
revised_comments: Several institutions in the Republic of Congo offer tertiary ICT and STEM programmes. Marien Ngouabi University, the country's main public university, provides computer science (informatique) and engineering degrees, including electronics and telecommunications through its National School of Polytechnic Studies (ENSP). Additional providers include the Congo University of Science and Technology, Denis Sassou Nguesso University, and private institutions such as the Higher Institute of Management and Technology (ISGT) and the Higher Institute of Technology of Central Africa (ISTAC), alongside the national engineering research institute INRSIIT. Enrolment data are not published, but the range of institutions indicates a moderate rather than negligible ICT/STEM education base.
